summary: Mixed ONNX-quantized and FP32 embeddings in rerank payload causing inconsistent scores and 502 errors
description:
Issue summary: Customer LumenDocs reported unstable reranking quality and intermittent 502s from our rerank endpoint during a nightly ingestion job. The rerank step receives a mix of embeddings generated by two pipelines (an older FP32 pipeline and a newer ONNX quantized pipeline).

Impact: Several scoring requests returned 502s for batches that included mixed-dimension vectors; other requests returned valid responses but with unexpectedly low cosine similarity scores causing irrelevant top-k results. Customer reported production regression in search relevance and elevated error rate on their dedicated capacity cluster.

Observed at: 2026-03-10 02:14 - first error spike; sustained increased error rate during customer's nightly run (02:00–04:00 UTC).

Why this matters: The reranker assumes homogeneous vector dimensions and normalization semantics. Mixing quantized ONNX outputs (1536 dims, asymmetric quantization and different post-normalization) with FP32 outputs (1024 dims, L2-normalized) produced shape mismatches and incorrect dot-product math when batch-scored on the GPU path, causing runtime exceptions and silent score distortions when shapes were coerced.
reproduction_steps:
1) Customer reproducer: run embed pipeline A (text-embed-1024-fp32-v1) for half the corpus and pipeline B (text-embed-1536-quant8-onnx-v2) for the other half.
2) Submit batched rerank request with interleaved candidate vectors from both pipelines.
3) Observe 502s in ~18% of batches and non-deterministic low similarity scores in successful batches.
4) Local repro by support: used customer sample bundle + mix script attached (see confluence) to produce identical stack traces and score anomalies.
logs:
Example stack trace (serving-runtime):
RuntimeError: matmul(): size mismatch, m1: [128,1536], m2: [1024,1024] at serving_runtime/ops/attention.cpp:412
Request id: req_8f7b2a3c
Reranker error context: batch_index=27, candidate_count=128, model=rerank-score-lite-v1
Gateway: 502 Bad Gateway returned by reranker service; upstream error: 1.7s timeout triggered after worker exit.
Customer reproduction log sample attached to ticket (log bundle id: lumendocs-20260310-02).
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: dimension mismatch only. Deep dive found two correlated root causes: (1) Customer SDK rollout accidentally toggled a new ONNX quantized exporter for part of their pipeline, producing 1536-d vectors; (2) Our reranker accepts mixed-dimension payloads and attempts to pad/truncate silently in one codepath, which produced incorrect numerical results when quantized vectors were padded.

Key findings:
- The embeddings-service accepted both vectors without schema validation (no dim enforcement) when submitted via multipart batch.
- The GPU scoring path asserts equal dims; when that assert was bypassed in a fallback path, we tried a CPU pad-and-score path that produced incorrect normalization semantics.
- Quantized ONNX vectors arrived scaled differently (post-quantization scale factors not reversed) causing cosine scores to shrink even when shapes matched.

Evidence & links:
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/lumen/embedding-errors?from=now-3h&to=now
- Reproducer PR with sample mixed-payload: github.com/lumendocs/repro/commit/24a7c1
- Serving logs referenced above.

resolution:
Hotfix: added strict embedding-dimension validation at the embeddings-service boundary to reject mixed-dimension batches with 400 and descriptive error. Fixed serving-runtime to fail fast (400) instead of causing 502s when shapes differ. Deployed PRs: embeddings-service#889, serving-runtime#2154. Customer temporarily rolled back ONNX export to FP32 pipeline while fix deployed.

Follow-ups:
- Create alert rule for sudden increase in 'embedding-dimension-mismatch' telemetry (SRE task).
- Update SDK docs to call out dimensions and provide migration checklist (Docs task).
- Outreach: CS to schedule postmortem call with LumenDocs and offer 30 days of waived overage credits for disrupted nightly jobs.
next_steps:
1) Add schema enforcement unit tests and CI gate for embeddings-service PR pipeline.
2) Product to publish embedding migration guide and prepare a compatibility page for quantized exporters.
3) Support to add knowledge base article with recommended remediation steps and SDK upgrade notes.
notes_for_engineering: Ensure quantization exporter includes explicit metadata (vector_dimension, scale_factors, normalization) in embedding payload. Prefer rejecting unknown exporter metadata rather than silently accepting. Consider a migration mode that converts quantized vectors server-side only if safe and opt-in.
